children: Hotter-than-expected inflation data sent U.S. stock indexes lower on Wednesday, but one sector was broadly resisting the slump.

Big Pharma led the S&P 500 on a generally down day for the market as the three major indexes traded in the red. Eli Lilly, the world's largest drugmaker by market value, rallied 3.6% to $1,208. Shares moved above their 50-day moving average to mark their highest level since late August.

Merck and AbbVie showed equally strong momentum. Merck, too, climbed above its 50-day moving average on Wednesday, with shares ultimately finishing up 3.8% at $5.39. AbbVie, meanwhile, advanced 3.3% to $283.48 to notch a record close.

The rally wasn't driven by a company-specific catalyst; rather, it was triggered by September's Consumer Price Index (CPI) reading. The CPI, a measure of U.S. goods and services costs, rose by 0.6% month over month in September. That pushed the 12-month rate to 3.7%, marking a sharp acceleration from 3.4% in August.

The resulting risk-off sentiment sent investors piling back into healthcare. Historically, the sector has acted as a defensive haven during broader market volatility and a primary destination for anti-tech rotations — a trend that has gained traction in recent months.
As recently as June, investors rotated away from artificial-intelligence stocks and into value and defensive sectors, notably healthcare, industrials, and financials.

Other notable gainers Wednesday included Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer, Amgen, and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals. Reflecting broad-based strength across the group, the iShares U.S. Pharmaceuticals exchange-traded fund advanced 2.5% on Wednesday.
Health insurers weren't missing out on the rally, either. Industry leader UnitedHealth Group climbed 4.7% to $395.62, ending the session as the biggest gainer in the S&P 500.
